A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPGym and provide readable main text, appendices, equations, figures, and tables. Retained material can be matched across the extensive reorganization. Internal reporting inconsistencies affect interpretation but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original RL training, generalization, augmentation, and puzzle-size experiments in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and adds augmented-image generalization, ground-truth state controls, and representation probing experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: SPGym's image-pool procedure, transitions, reward, and initialization methods remain unchanged. The agent architectures and learning objectives are retained across v3 Appendices A/F and v4 Appendices B/A.1. One-hot observations were already supported; their new evaluation and the diagnostic probes do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v4 substantially broadens evaluated input conditions through Easy OOD tests on augmented training images and ground-truth one-hot observations, alongside a new puzzle-state prediction task for linear probes. ImageNet, DiffusionDB, and both 3x3 and 4x4 puzzles were already used in v3.

E2.justification: The core visual-agent roster remains unchanged. Within specific comparisons, v4 adds SAC and DreamerV3 to the puzzle-size and continued-training analyses previously reported only for PPO, and introduces one-hot counterparts as controls in Table 9. These extend comparisons using the existing algorithm families.

E3.justification: New protocols include 100 evaluation episodes per augmentation type for Easy OOD, frozen-encoder classifiers predicting puzzle states, and one-hot controls using two-layer PPO/SAC MLPs and DreamerV3's three-layer MLP. Augmentation searches expand beyond RAD, and Section 5.2 reports preliminary 10,000–20,000-image pools. The principal image-based training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds substantial diagnostics testing whether representation quality predicts sample efficiency, how removing pixel representation learning affects performance, and whether agents tolerate simple visual perturbations. Augmentation sensitivity expands from RAD to RAD/CURL/SPR, and the early-stopping analysis expands from PPO to SAC and DreamerV3.

E5.justification: v4 adds Pearson correlation analyses with significance reporting for Easy OOD performance versus sample efficiency and probe accuracy versus sample efficiency, reporting r=-0.81 with p=2.5e-12 and p=1.1e-13 respectively. Five-seed evaluation and mean plus/minus 1.96 standard errors are retained; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: v4 adds Easy OOD, probing, one-hot, and expanded grid-size/continued-training results. PPO's 4x4 report changes from 51.4% success after 10M steps to 24.46M steps to 80% success, rather than a comparable fixed-budget gain. Some revised main-table values conflict with retained appendix results: DBC at pool 10 is 2.13M in v4 Table 1 but remains 10.00M in Tables 10/12 and v3 Table 5. DreamerV3's tabulated OOD results are removed.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, normalized Manhattan-distance reward in Equations 1–2, and auxiliary learning objectives in Equations 3–8 are mathematically retained. Added pool notation and explanatory wording do not introduce new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a controlled visual RL benchmark, evaluation of existing methods, and identification of scaling limitations. v4 adds headline claims linking representation quality to performance and highlighting poorer perturbation robustness with larger training pools. Its conclusion more explicitly attributes generalization failure to memorization.

C2.justification: v4 develops new explanations involving network-capacity exhaustion, weak learning signals under extreme diversity, and task-specific invariances learned from smaller pools. It adds qualifications about pretraining comparison fairness and imperfect separation of representation learning from policy learning. The original limitations concerning minimal tuning and five seeds remain.

D1.justification: v4 documents the new one-hot encoder configurations and frozen-encoder probe procedure, and clarifies that sample-efficiency measurements are averaged across parallel environments before seeds. Existing architecture listings, hyperparameter tables, hardware, runtimes, and code-access information are largely retained and relocated into Appendix A.

R1.justification: v4 adds CARLA and COOM to benchmark positioning and introduces background citations including Bengio, Lesort, Mnih, and the Yarats augmentation paper. The principal positioning against existing visual and puzzle benchmarks remains. DreamerV3 and deterministic-autoencoder reference updates correspond to publication updates, rather than newly introduced methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, results, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Five research-question passages become seven numbered results subsections. Appendices A–F are reorganized into setup/configuration, algorithms, and supplementary analyses, with widespread terminology changes emphasizing visual diversity.

P2.justification: Main result tables are redesigned around multiple pool sizes, and v3's comprehensive Table 5 is split into algorithm-specific Tables 11–13. v4 adds one-hot and probe tables, expands the augmentation comparison to three panels, and removes the text example from the observation illustration. The DiffusionDB plot moves to the appendix; many other learning curves are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, the new state controls, probes, and Easy OOD tests provide more direct validation of the benchmark's purpose. However, v4 introduces conflicting sample-efficiency values between Table 1 and Tables 10/12, claims DreamerV3 outperforms all SAC variants despite faster RAD results, and contradicts itself about DreamerV3 OOD evaluation in Section 5.3 versus Appendix C.2. These substantive additions and new reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
